C3: That the driver had not 'arrived' is not a ground to waive the fee: the driver was in fact within 39 m of the pickup by 08:46:10 and had been within 200 m since 08:41:25 (5 min 15 s), and Ryde publishes no rule allowing a rider to cancel free of charge because the driver's ETA was not met, so the rider's only remedy is a discretionary RydeHELP appeal under NS-7. [F1 F2] [NS-4 NS-7]

The rider cancelled at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s (400 s) after acceptance at 08:40:00 [F4], i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 fee is chargeable [F4][F7][NS-0][NS-4]. The driver was first within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:25, accumulated 5 min 15 s within 200 m before the cancellation, and was closest at 39 m at 08:46:10 [F1][F2][F5]. claims.assertion: This is a rider cancellation of an instant booking (RydeX, Raffles Place → Sentosa Beach Station), so the fee turns on NS-4: the rider cancelled at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after acceptance at 08:40:00, i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is valid under NS-0/NS-4.

The rider's own messages show the cancellation was purely voluntary ('Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' at 08:45); no driver conduct, no-show claim by the driver, or safety event is in issue, so NS-1/NS-2 do not arise.

That the driver had not 'arrived' is not a ground to waive the fee: the driver was in fact within 39 m of the pickup by 08:46:10 and had been within 200 m since 08:41:25 (5 min 15 s), and Ryde publishes no rule allowing a rider to cancel free of charge because the driver's ETA was not met, so the rider's only remedy is a discretionary RydeHELP appeal under NS-7.

Even if the driver's NS-1 prerequisites are checked, the record shows a platform-recorded arrival at 08:41:25 and a driver 'I'm Here' tap at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup, with continuous presence within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap and cancellation 5 min 15 s after arrival — so the $6.61 fee would equally stand on the driver's side of NS-1; the rider does not contest the fee on its merits.

No mitigating traffic or weather excuse exists on the record and none is needed, since the cancellation was the rider's choice; the fare record shows no surge (1.0×) so the fee is the standard published $6.61 amount and no ERP or other unbilled item is added under FARE-1.

weaknesses: The time facts defeat the rider's fairness argument outright: acceptance 08:40:00 and cancellation 08:46:40 (F4) is well past the 3-minute window, so NS-4 says the $6.61 stands; the rider's complaint that 'the driver had not even arrived' is contradicted by F1 (39 m at 08:46:10) and F2 (within 200 m from 08:41:25).

The rider never claims the driver did anything wrong, and F10 ('Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel') is an admission of a purely voluntary cancellation, so no exemption clause (RD/SAFE/NS-1/NS-2) is available.

The rider cannot invoke any driver-side fault to shift the fee: F5/F6 show a platform arrival record and a valid 'I'm Here' tap inside 200 m (F3, F6), and the driver's 90-day history (F17: 2 no-show disputes, 2 upheld) would only reinforce that the no-show process was followed here.
Profile facts (F16: rider 1 dispute in 90 d, 0 upheld) cannot carry the case either way and give no basis for a flag_account request against the driver.

claims.assertion: The rider — not the driver — cancelled this trip: the timeline records "Cancelled by rider at 08:46:40", so the fee question is governed by NS-0/NS-4 (rider cancellation of an instant job), not by the no-show branch.
The rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance at 08:40:00, i.e. well beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable under NS-4.

The driver did in fact arrive and wait: he first came within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:25 and accumulated 5 min 15 s within 200 m before the cancellation, contradicting the rider's assertion that he "had not even arrived".
The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point and remained within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, satisfying every element of NS-1 (i)–(iii) on the system record.

The driver was stationary at the pickup from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40, 41 m from the pickup point, so the wait was continuous and covered to the moment of cancellation; his written statement to the same effect is corroborated by GPS and is not a bare assertion.

The rider's own message at 08:45 states her reason was "plans changed" and that she would cancel — a voluntary, reasonless cancellation unrelated to driver conduct or delay, which is exactly the situation NS-4 prices at $6.61.

No ground of driver fault exists to reduce the fee: there were no traffic incidents or congestion bands on the route and the weather was fair, so no reroute or delay of the driver's making is in the record.
The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so the timing of the driver's arrival message and the rider's cancellation message can be relied on without any G12 gap.
The $6.61 on the fare record is the published, un-surged cancellation fee (multiplier 1.0×) — a disclosed charge, not an unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 is not engaged.

The fee was raised 6 min 40 s after acceptance, well inside the 30-day dispute window, so the rider's filing is timely; the driver nonetheless asks that the fee stand because every condition of NS-1 is met on the system record.

The driver's 90-day record shows 613 trips, a 4.81 rating and only 2 upheld no-show disputes against 613 trips, which is not a repeated-violation pattern and provides no basis for any account flag against him in this case.

weaknesses: The rider will point to F16 (her clean 90-day record: 1 dispute, 0 upheld) to argue she is a good-faith rider who cancelled for a genuine change of plans, not to game the fee.

Strictly, NS-1(i)–(iii) is the rider-no-show branch; here the cancellation is the rider's own (F4), so the primary basis is NS-4, and the driver relies on NS-1's arrival/waiting conditions only as supporting evidence — a judge may prefer to decide on NS-4 alone and give the NS-1 evidence less weight.

The driver's 08:42 message (F9) announces his arrival but the rider never replies before cancelling at 08:46:40 (F10, F11); the rider may argue she could not locate the car in a busy Raffles Place pickup area, making her "had not even arrived" complaint arguable even though GPS (F2, F3) contradicts it.

The driver's written statement (F12) is self-serving; it only helps because GPS (F3) independently corroborates it, and it would be discarded if the trajectory had a coverage gap — no gap is shown in the index, but the record does not affirmatively certify the track covers 08:42–08:46:40 continuously beyond F3's stationary window.

Not contested: F11 records two timestamped messages with no gap, so the timing of F9 and F10 is reliable and no G12 incompleteness arises; note the incompleteness would not help the rider anyway, as the record still shows a post-window cancellation (F4).

Conceded; the rider's 08:45 message and 08:46:40 cancellation (F10, F4) are the only remaining fact of note — the dispute is timely but timeliness does not create a substantive ground to waive the fee.

The rider has never sought a flag against the driver and does not do so now; I agree F17's 613 trips and 4.81 rating give no repeated-violation pattern for a flag_account under RD-6 in a rider-cancellation case.

My own C3 stands as the rider's only residual avenue and is stated honestly: because F1/F2 show the driver did arrive and Ryde publishes no ETA-delay waiver (no such rule exists to cite under NS-4), the fee stands and the rider's remedy is a discretionary RydeHELP voucher appeal under NS-7, not a ruling.
